svg.title: Four Seats at Base; Six at Scale
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-four-to-six-person-pod; chart type: org_architecture; title: Four Seats at Base; Six at Scale; subtitle: One accountable fleet lead coordinates three contractors before adding two distinct expansion seats.; chapter number: 11; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: FT means full-time seat; C means contractor seat. Conservative and Base use 1 FT + 3 C, four people total. Scaled uses 2 FT + 4 C, six people total. Each node represents one person; the last two nodes activate only in the Scaled configuration. Seat labels do not determine worker classification.; caption: Conservative: $180,000 gross, $99,000 retained, $25,200 profit at 14% gross margin and 25.45% retained margin. Base: $690,000 gross, $379,500 retained, $144,900 profit at 21.0% and 38.18%. Scaled: $1,200,000 gross, $660,000 retained, $336,000 profit at 28% and 50.91%. Scaled economics require the six-person pod.; stages: label: Fleet principal — base FT; value: One full-time owner leads contracts, cash, and exception decisions; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Own vehicle acceptance, insurer relationships, investor terms, weekly contribution review, and incident escalation. Approve settlement corrections against source evidence rather than allowing dispatch to rewrite owner allocations.; label: Dispatch coordinator — base contractor; value: One contractor coordinates assignments, handovers, and driver communication; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Maintain the vehicle availability board, collect signed handover records, route platform issues, and confirm service interruptions. Escalate coverage and permit exceptions instead of assigning around them.; label: Maintenance coordinator — base contractor; value: One contractor schedules inspections, repairs, and downtime recovery; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Review OBD-II alerts, mileage intervals, tire condition, repair estimates, and return-to-service evidence. Keep maintenance availability separate from paid utilization so idle vehicles remain visible.; label: Settlement specialist — base contractor; value: One contractor reconciles billing, tolls, and investor statements; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Match platform exports, bank receipts, owner splits, repair invoices, and toll evidence. Produce aged receivables and deposit-liability schedules; the fleet principal reviews adjustments and payment releases.; label: Operations manager — scaled FT; value: Add one full-time manager only in the six-person configuration; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Take daily dispatch supervision and service recovery from the principal. Use documented workload, incident response, and contribution capacity to justify the seat rather than hiring against gross passenger fare volume.; label: Claims and onboarding specialist — scaled contractor; value: Add one contractor for screening administration and incident documentation; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Assemble authorized screening records, renewal evidence, collision photographs, insurer submissions, and recovery tracking. Keep report access restricted and separate claims documentation from settlement payment authority.
